newsitem.title: UK: Czarnikow sees lower Ukraine 1996 sugar output.
newsitem.headline: Czarnikow sees lower Ukraine 1996 sugar output.

text.p: Ukraine's sugar output could reach 2.70 million tonnes white value in 1996, 100,000 tonnes lower than the official estimate, as adverse weather becomes more of a risk to harvesting operations, Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.

In its latest monthly report, Czarnikow said output in Ukraine -- eastern Europe's largest sugar producer -- only amounted to 2.38 million tonnes by the end of November, compared with 3.16 million tonnes by the same date last year.
"Production in 1995 finished just short of 3.5 million tonnes and if similar end-season performance were seen this year, output in 96 would close at around 2.7 million tonnes," the report said.
Almost half the country's beet factories had closed by this time, it added.
Czarnikow noted that other industry sources were even more pessimistic about Ukraine's crop prospects and were forecasting total sugar output as low as 2.6 million tonnes for 1996.
